title: Forms of government in Ethiopia
competency: List and describe the forms of government in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: The military regime of 1974–1991; the word means committee.
A form of government where the state is ruled by citizens' representatives chosen in periodic elections.

en.text: Ethiopia had a monarchy until 1974: absolute, centralized and unitary, with the throne passed to the emperor's descendants under the 1931 Constitution. The Derg (1974–1991) was a military, unitary regime that replaced feudalism with socialism and set up the National Shengo. Since 1991 Ethiopia has been a federal republic with a parliamentary system.

screens.title: The 1931 Constitution
screens.ask: Under the 1931 Constitution, who did sovereign power belong to?
screens.after: The Emperor. People had subject status. Power flowed down from the king.

screens.title: A. The monarchy
paras: The imperial system lasted until 1974. It was absolute and centralized.
Article 4 of the 1931 Constitution passed the throne to the emperor's descendants.
Sovereignty was vested in the Emperor; he made and enforced laws.
There was a two-chamber parliament, but the emperor controlled law-making and nominated senators.

screens.title: B. The military regime (Derg)
paras: The Derg ended the long feudal system.
It was a military and dictatorial government with a unitary structure.
It replaced feudalism with socialism and the monarchy with a presidential system, ending succession by descent.
A one-chamber parliament, the National Shengo, was formed; the president was head of state and commander-in-chief.

screens.title: C. The post-1991 republic
paras: The Derg was deposed in May 1991.
Ethiopia adopted a republican form of government with a parliamentary system.
A republic is ruled by citizens' representatives chosen in free, fair, periodic elections.
screens.note: The book notes elections have been held since 1991, with complaints of one-party dominance, election rigging and corruption.
